newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek Avax to up capital by 2.1 bln drs.
newsitem.headline: Greek Avax to up capital by 2.1 bln drs.

text.p: Greek construction firm Avax got shareholder approval for a 2.064 billion drachma rights issue and will issue 1.72 million new common registered shares with a par value of 150 drachmas at 1,200 each.
The terms will be four new shares per 10 outstanding.

Management told the annual general shareholder assembly on Friday that nearly half of the rights issue proceeds would be chanelled to the Attiki Odos BOT project, known as the Stavros-Elefsis ring road, where Avax claims a 6.9 percent stake.
A third of the proceeds will be used for working capital needs and the purchase of equipment.
The balance will be invested in real estate and the BOOT project in Moldova for construction of a port terminal and fuel and LPG storage facilities.
A total of 1.65 billion drachmas would be received in 1997 due to a budget revision in the Athens subway project, shareholders were told.
Avax will launch a three-year investment plan spanning to 1999 budgeted at 4.0 billion drachmas which includes the wrap up of fixed asset investments, management said.
Investments in 1995 and 1996 totalled 1.47 billion drachmas.
Avax's pre-tax earnings increased 14.2 percent to 1.524 billion drachmas on turnover growth of 28.9 percent to 8.521 billion drachmas in 1996.
Management expects 1997 corporate results to register a 30 percent increase on 1996.
As of the end of 1996, the uncompleted portion of Avax's order book amounted to 42.4 billion drachmas versus 15.0 billion a year earlier.
Six projects budgeted at 3.25 billion were signed in 1997, management said.
Avax upped its dividend per share to 110 drachmas for fiscal 1996 from 100 in the previous year. The last cum-div day was May 16, 1997.
Avax's shares closed 40 drachmas up at 2,480 on Friday on volume of 44,960 shares. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
